proposed_title: HCP reports July consumer prices down month-on-month and year-on-year
what_happened: A fresh Cloud HTTPS GET retrieved HCP's exact 19 August 2026 release. HCP reports that Morocco's consumer price index fell 1.0% from June to July 2026 and 0.6% from July 2025; these are official statistical results, not an independent assessment of household welfare.
key_facts: OFFICIAL_CLAIM: HCP reports a 1.0% month-on-month CPI decrease in July 2026, comprising a 1.9% food-index decrease and a 0.3% non-food decrease.
OFFICIAL_CLAIM: HCP reports a 0.6% year-on-year CPI decrease, with food down 3.7% and non-food up 1.9%.
OFFICIAL_CLAIM: HCP reports that Meknes CPI fell 1.0% month-on-month.
UNKNOWN: the release alone does not establish changes in household purchasing power, incomes or living standards.

primary_sources.claim_supported: HCP's national, category and city CPI changes for July 2026
primary_sources.independence: Official national statistical producer; no independent household-outcome inference is made

independent_sources.attribution: Morocco World News report tracing the figures to HCP
independent_sources.claim_supported: Independent publication trail for the reported July CPI movements
independent_sources.independence: Editorially separate report, but it relies on the same HCP release and is not an independent statistical estimate

contradictory_evidence: A falling aggregate CPI does not mean every price fell or that every household experienced the same change.
The same release reports non-food prices 1.9% higher year-on-year even while the overall index fell.
uncertainty: High confidence in what the retrieved HCP release reports; household-level effects and causal explanations were not established.
context: This packet stays narrowly within the official release. Any broader cost-of-living story requires independent distributional and income evidence.
why_it_matters: The release provides a current, dated inflation indicator and shows materially different food and non-food movements.
strategic_angle: BRIEF with explicit HCP attribution; do not generalize the index into a welfare claim.
